g.text: Thursday 23 July, 10:10. Varma has not forgotten April. Three days of tracing, a compacted history, and
a summary that kept the amounts and lost which account paid which.
"It summarised the trail into a list of numbers," she says. "Tell me that cannot happen again."
You cannot tell her that about a paragraph the model writes freely. You can about a form.
Okafor drafts it on the whiteboard as he would a schedule: payer, payee, total, count, the statement it
came from. Open questions. Accounts read.
"If a line has no payer," he says, "it is not a line."
lantern.compaction.SCHEMA, as the model is asked to fill it in
Every flow needs all five fields. The check compares each one with the tool result it came from, kept in a
ledger outside the window, and names what is missing or wrong.
A paragraph: what each compaction kept
the last paragraph LANTERN wrote for itself
FLOW: Osprey Point Management Ltd -> Tidewater Holdings Trust | 8 payments | total 1861000.00
flows were whole. The trace then reported
forms refused. Every form that was kept had every flow whole:
. The form filled in by code
The same checked trace, four ways of compacting it
The last row has no model in the compaction at all: the form is built from the ledger of tool results. It
cannot drop a payer, and it cannot record an open question, because nothing in a tool result is a question.
Compacted to a paragraph whenever it passed 1,500 tokens, the trace was compacted 2 times; after the
last, 1 of the 8 flows the tools had returned were still whole, and the report held 1 of 7 hops with 1
totals right. With a form checked in code, 0 forms were refused and the report held 0 hops with 0 totals
right. With the form filled in by code from the tool results, 0 hops and 0 totals right, in 16,194
tokens where the uncompacted trace took 23,899.
